strengths: Strong empirical results with consistent +10.1 average improvement across four diverse personalized detection benchmarks, verified with statistical significance tests (p < 10^-17)
Comprehensive experimental methodology including oracle experiments, ablation studies, dimensionality analysis, and qualitative visualizations that effectively validate design choices
Well-designed three-stage approach combining multimodal supervision, feature translation via attention+MLP, and dual-objective loss for both local alignment and geometric regularization
Practical system requiring no teacher at inference with minimal overhead, suitable for resource-constrained deployment on mobile robotics and edge devices
Clear presentation with informative figures, detailed pseudocode, comprehensive appendix, and toy example effectively illustrating the embedding loss mechanism
Technically sound methodology with clever PCA-based dimensionality reduction incorporating power-law normalization for channel balancing
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (knowledge distillation, translation modules, PCA compression, relational embedding regularization) are established techniques; contribution is primarily their combination rather than introduction of new concepts

Incremental improvements over closely related prior work AuXFT: when initialized from AuXFT weights (fairest comparison), MOCHA achieves only +4.9 points; the three claimed differences (multimodal supervision, compact embeddings, explicit regularization) lack isolated validation of their individual contributions

Multimodal supervision analysis is shallow: Table 1 shows multimodal fusion helps but does not explain why; fusion approach (Eq. 1) with γ = ||h_i|| normalization is ad-hoc; no ablation separately measuring visual versus textual contributions; no comparison with alternative fusion strategies

Narrow evaluation scope limited to four specialized personalized detection benchmarks without evaluation on standard detection benchmarks (COCO test, ImageNet), preventing assessment of whether improvements generalize beyond niche personalized scenarios

Training computational cost not properly addressed: paper acknowledges 'significant computational cost' from foundation models but provides no numbers; 48 hours on 8 GPUs is substantial yet no comparison with baseline training costs, creating potential unfairness if baselines are cheaper to train

Few-shot learning limited to prototypical networks only; no comparison with other FSL methods; acknowledged limitation that prototype classifier is 'inefficient at large scales' limits practical applicability; evaluation with only 1-5 support samples is artificial

Missing critical analyses: no error analysis or failure modes; no explanation of dataset-specific performance variations (why MOCHA helps more on PerSeg/POD); no quantification of inference overhead from translation module; insufficient detail on teacher feature extraction (token averaging for h_i unclear)

Reproducibility gaps: hyperparameter values (λ_dist, λ_emb) not specified; exact teacher inference procedure incompletely detailed; code availability not mentioned; some implementation details ambiguous (how frozen teacher processes boxes)

Technical justifications lacking: PCA power-law fitting appears post-hoc without principled explanation; choice of L1+L2 loss versus alternatives not justified; temperature τ selection not discussed; translation module design not compared to alternatives
Oracle experiments suggest strong initialization from AuXFT weights is crucial (+3.7 point boost), raising questions about fair comparison; unclear if all baselines use identical initialization

strengths: Strong and consistent experimental results across 4 personalization benchmarks (+10.1% avg over baseline, +4.9% over AuXFT) with statistical significance testing (Wilcoxon p < 10^-17)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including oracle experiments, extensive ablations on PCA dimensionality/components/student architectures/FSL classifiers, and qualitative analysis
Practical efficiency at inference (only ~3ms overhead, ~10% relative increase) with detailed implementation details and pseudocode supporting reproducibility

Well-motivated dual-objective distillation design combining local alignment (L_dist) and global relational consistency (L_emb), with effective toy experiment (Fig. 3) demonstrating geometric preservation
Clear presentation with informative visualizations (Fig. 2 system overview, Fig. 5 feature similarity, qualitative results) and thorough appendix with statistical validation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (L1+L2 loss, softmax relational loss, transformer encoder, PCA) are standard; novelty lies primarily in combination rather than new techniques
Training-time computational cost contradicts efficiency narrative: requires LLaVa-1.5-7B for 11-28 hours of distillation, undermining the core efficiency motivation despite fast inference

Significant generalization concerns: gains diminish dramatically with model scale (YOLOv8n: +10.1% → RT-DETR-l: +2.1%), suggesting method tailored to CNN multi-scale hierarchies rather than transformer architectures

Limited scope and evaluation: restricted to object detection only; personalization datasets contain visually similar objects with limited scale diversity; different metrics across datasets (mAP vs. retrieval accuracy) complicate interpretation

Incomplete analysis of multimodal knowledge learned: only LLaVa tested as teacher (no other VLMs explored); feature similarity visualization (Fig. 5) is superficial; no failure case analysis or investigation of when/why method outperforms baselines
Acknowledged scalability limitations not addressed: prototypical networks inefficient at scale with many personalized classes (A.6); no proposed solutions for large-scale deployment scenarios

Technical design choices lack justification: rescaling factor γ = ||h_i|| appears arbitrary; power-law PCA normalization (σ ≃ a/(x+1)^b + c) fitting lacks theoretical grounding; limited ablation on design alternatives

Reproducibility and implementation gaps: code availability not mentioned; translator architecture details sparse (attention heads, FFN dims, dropout); distillation dataset composition not fully specified; λ coefficient selection process unclear
